1.why: Recovery verification requires the record’s sessionId to match the caller’s session and the submitted code to match the stored bcrypt token hash bound to that recovery request.

2.why: The same code cannot be used from another session because recovery-verify enforces record.sessionId === session.id and per-record token hash checks.

3.why: Password reset updates accountPasswordHash and the current session only; no other sessions are invalidated or logged out.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and responses send HSTS, so the app is served over HTTPS.

5.why: Reset tokens and passwords are protected with bcrypt hashing (not classical encryption); no separate encryption of other user data at rest.

6.why: No real email body is sent; the user-facing recovery message is generic and does not echo private account fields, though testToken is returned in the API for the demo.

7.why: Inputs pass through cleanText/validIdentifier/validPassword, which bound length and reject control characters and <>.

8.why: Navigation uses a fixed in-app hash allowlist and API next paths are relative internal routes only, with no open external redirects.

9.why: There is no email template rendering of user input; client rendering escapes dynamic text via esc().

10.why: Error JSON is generic and server catch hides stacks, but recovery/MFA tokens are returned as testToken/testMfaCode and written to the on-page logs.

11.why: Runtime password storage uses bcrypt, yet the initial password plaintext and MFA_TEST_CODE are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: The demo accepts fixed default credentials helena@hospital.test / Welcome!2025Heart.

13.why: Login, recovery-request, recovery-verify, and MFA paths throttle or lock after repeated failures.

14.why: Login and recovery-request messages are generic, but a non-existent account can still be distinguished at the password step after code verification.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte randomBytes values (base64url), hashed at rest, and bound to the requesting session/recovery record.
